title: Listening tastes broadened beyond New Orleans
summary: He enjoys listening as much as ever, now appreciates New Orleans, Chicago, Ellington, blues and folk artists.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Right. Yeah, it is a distressing thing.
Do you enjoy listening, uh, as, we won't say as much, that's hard to gauge, but do you enjoy listening as you did years ago?

Oh, yes. Every, every bit as much. I, I still, you know, buy records as reissues and things that come out, you know. Mm-hmm. I, I listen as much as I ever did and I guess I maybe appreciate a lot of things that I didn't used to.
In other words, you feel that, knowledgeably, you're farther ahead with every year. Mm-hmm.

Yeah. Yeah, I love jazz as much as I ever did. Still, uh, in a, a New Orleans groove? Uh, yes. Well, I, my tastes have broadened. I mean, uh, I went through a period, you know, first I would like nothing except authentic New Orleans jazz and, and then I broke away from that and I wanted nothing except, uh, authentic, if there is such a thing, authentic Chicago style jazz. And now my tastes are broad enough that I can listen to both and get something from it. Mm-hmm.
Uh, do you go, uh, uh, uh, do you cover a broader span? Do you listen to Ellington or do you listen to...
Oh, yes, yes. Yes, Ellington and, uh, you know, I like all kinds of things. I collect tapes of the Mills Blue Rhythm Orchestra and all.
Mainly, uh, instrumental. Uh, yes, but some vocal stuff.

I, you know, I like Bessie Smith and, uh, I even like, uh, a lot of folk artists, uh, you know, uh, jazz, basically jazz folk artists like Lightning Hopkins. Uh, I like Lead Belly and, uh, Leroy Carr and a lot of, a lot of people like that, you know. A lot of things I didn't used to listen to that I got a great deal of pleasure from now.
